prompt.en: Findlay says Paul builds Christian liberty on the ruins of confuted ____.
prompt.es: Findlay dice que Pablo edifica la libertad cristiana sobre las ruinas del ____ refutado.

questions.source_quote: On the ruins of confuted legalism he builds up an impregnable fortress for Christian liberty, an immortal vindication of the gospel of the grace of God.

prompt.en: The freedom of which group does Findlay say was bound up with Paul's position at this crisis? The ____ believers.
prompt.es: ¿La libertad de qué grupo, según Findlay, estaba ligada a la posición de Pablo en esta crisis? Los creyentes ____.

questions.source_quote: The cause of Gentile freedom at this crisis was bound up with the person of the Apostle Paul.

prompt.en: Findlay explains that Paul was defending his ____ against malicious attacks, not merely narrating his biography.
prompt.es: Findlay explica que Pablo defendía su ____ frente a ataques maliciosos, no solo narraba su biografía.

questions.source_quote: In the eyes of his children in the faith, he is bound to vindicate his Apostolic character, defamed by Jewish malice and untruth.

prompt.en: Findlay calls Paul, at this crisis, the ____ and stay of the truth.
prompt.es: Findlay describe a Pablo, en esa crisis, como la ____ y el sostén de la verdad.

questions.source_quote: He was himself just now "the pillar and stay of the truth."

prompt.en: Findlay argues that the superhuman origin of Paul's message made the gospel ____.
prompt.es: Findlay sostiene que el origen sobrehumano del mensaje de Pablo hacía al evangelio ____.

questions.source_quote: The gospel of Paul was inviolable, then, because of its superhuman character.

prompt.en: Findlay refuses to make Paul an apostle at ____ dependent upon Jerusalem's pillars.
prompt.es: Findlay se niega a presentar a Pablo como apóstol ____ dependiente de las columnas de Jerusalén.

questions.source_quote: He is no Apostle at second-hand, no disciple of Peter's or dependant of the "pillars" at Jerusalem.

prompt.en: In Findlay's account, the gulf in Paul's life could only be bridged by supernatural ____.
prompt.es: En la exposición de Findlay, el abismo entre las etapas de la vida de Pablo solo podía salvarse mediante una ____ sobrenatural.

questions.source_quote: The chasm between his Christian and pre-Christian life had only been bridged by a supernatural interposition of the mercy of Christ.

prompt.en: For Findlay, an ____ vision was the means of opening Saul's heart, rather than merely a subjective idea.
prompt.es: Para Findlay, una visión ____ fue el medio para abrir el corazón de Saulo, no simplemente una idea subjetiva.

questions.source_quote: The objective vision could only have revealed a "Christ after the flesh," had it not been the means of opening Saul's closed heart to the influence of the Spirit of Christ.

prompt.en: Findlay explicitly denies that Paul's self-assertion in Antioch came from personal ____.
prompt.es: Findlay niega expresamente que la defensa de Pablo en Antioquía naciera del ____ personal.

questions.source_quote: In his self-assertion there is no note of pride or personal anxiety.

prompt.en: Findlay calls the disputed passage a personal ____ of faith at a critical moment.
prompt.es: Findlay llama al pasaje controvertido una ____ personal de fe en un momento crítico.

questions.source_quote: Read in the light of the foregoing narrative, this passage is a compendium of the Pauline Gospel, invested with the peculiar interest that belongs to a confession of personal faith, made at a signal crisis in the author's life.

prompt.en: For Findlay, the decisive ____ used to expose Peter's dissimulation is the grace of God.
prompt.es: Para Findlay, la ____ decisiva para descubrir la simulación de Pedro es la gracia de Dios.

questions.source_quote: "The grace of God" is the touchstone to which Peter's dissimulation is finally brought.

prompt.en: Findlay defines divine grace more specifically than general affection: it is ____ love.
prompt.es: Findlay define la gracia divina como algo más preciso que el afecto general: es amor ____.

questions.source_quote: God's grace is not His love alone; it is redeeming love--love poured out upon the undeserving, love coming to seek and save the lost, "bringing salvation to all men" (Rom. v. 1-8; Tit. ii. 11).

prompt.en: Findlay describes divine grace as the ____ of human sin, overcoming rather than yielding to it.
prompt.es: Findlay describe la gracia divina como la ____ del pecado humano, que lo vence en vez de ceder ante él.

questions.source_quote: Grace in God is therefore the antithesis of sin in man, counterworking and finally triumphing over it.

prompt.en: Findlay portrays faith as the human ____ called forth by divine grace.
prompt.es: Findlay presenta la fe como la ____ humana suscitada por la gracia divina.

questions.source_quote: While sin is the reply which man's nature makes to the demands of law, faith is the response elicited by grace; it is the door of the heart opening to grace.[66] Grace and Faith go hand in hand, as Law and Transgression.

prompt.en: Findlay says the doctrine Paul defended was first the ____ of his own personal life.
prompt.es: Findlay dice que la doctrina defendida por Pablo era, ante todo, la ____ de su vida personal.

questions.source_quote: But it was, in the first place, the basis of his personal life.

prompt.en: Findlay describes the Spirit's ____ as binding together the glorified Lord and His earthly members.
prompt.es: Findlay describe la ____ del Espíritu como vínculo entre el Señor glorificado y sus miembros en la tierra.

questions.source_quote: The office of the Holy Spirit, whose communion holds together the glorified Lord and His members upon earth, is implied in the teaching of ver. 20.

prompt.en: Findlay says the Mosaic economy was ____ to the promise rather than a competing means of salvation.
prompt.es: Findlay dice que la economía mosaica era ____ respecto de la promesa y no un medio rival de salvación.

questions.source_quote: The Legal economy is ancillary thereto; it never professed to accomplish the work of grace, as the Judaists would have it do.

prompt.en: Findlay argues that Paul made the Law ____ to faith, not the perfection of it.
prompt.es: Findlay sostiene que Pablo hizo de la Ley algo ____ a la fe, no su perfeccionamiento.

questions.source_quote: They brought in the Law to perfect the unfinished work of faith (ver. 3): he made it preliminary and propædeutic.

prompt.en: In Findlay's medical comparison, bringing sin's disease to a crisis is a step toward its ____.
prompt.es: En la comparación médica de Findlay, llevar el mal del pecado a una crisis es un paso hacia su ____.

questions.source_quote: It aggravates the disease, in order to bring it to a crisis. And this is a necessary step towards the cure.

prompt.en: Findlay says that the Law prepared the ____ for the work of Grace.
prompt.es: Findlay afirma que la Ley preparó la ____ para la obra de la gracia.

questions.source_quote: It thus prepared the platform for the work of Grace.

prompt.en: Findlay first pictures God's heir in a period of ____ before possession of the estate.
prompt.es: Findlay presenta primero al heredero de Dios en su ____ antes de poseer la heredad.

questions.source_quote: We see, first, the heir of God in his minority; and again, the same heir in possession of his estate.

prompt.en: Findlay notes that civil ____ was fixed by law in Jewish and Roman societies.
prompt.es: Findlay señala que la ____ civil se fijaba por ley en las sociedades judía y romana.

questions.source_quote: In Roman and in Jewish law the date of civil majority was fixed.

prompt.en: In Findlay's analogy the father remains alive and keeps the heir in ____ until the appointed time.
prompt.es: En la analogía de Findlay el padre sigue vivo y mantiene al heredero bajo ____ hasta el momento señalado.

questions.source_quote: A grant is made by a father still living, who keeps his son in pupilage till he sees fit to put him in possession of the promised estate.

prompt.en: Findlay says Abraham's heritage emerged ____ after a long period of preparation.
prompt.es: Findlay afirma que la herencia de Abraham salió ____ después de una larga etapa de preparación.

questions.source_quote: The heritage of Abraham came into possession of his heirs enriched by their long minority.

prompt.en: Findlay says Paul's practical instructions defend the gospel from the charge of ____.
prompt.es: Findlay dice que las instrucciones prácticas de Pablo defienden el evangelio de la acusación de ____.

questions.source_quote: They vindicate Paul's gospel from the charge of antinomianism, while they guard Christians from giving occasion to the charge.

prompt.en: Findlay says liberty is especially perilous to a young, ____ nature.
prompt.es: Findlay dice que la libertad entraña especial peligro para una naturaleza joven y ____.

questions.source_quote: Here lies the danger of liberty, especially when conferred on a young, untrained nature, and in a newly emancipated community.

prompt.en: Although Findlay calls freedom priceless, he also calls it a grave ____.
prompt.es: Aunque Findlay considera preciosa la libertad, también la llama una grave ____.

questions.source_quote: Freedom is a priceless boon; but it is a grave responsibility.

prompt.en: Findlay says the natural man wants not the right to govern himself but the absence of ____.
prompt.es: Findlay dice que el hombre natural no quiere el derecho a gobernarse, sino la ausencia de ____.

questions.source_quote: The natural man defines freedom as the power to do as he likes; not the right of self-regulation, but the absence of regulation is what he desires.
questions.revision_note: v1c: answer changed from self-regulation to regulation; "self" repeated the digest answer self-control.

prompt.en: Findlay compares Paul's virtues with the four ____ virtues of classical philosophy.
prompt.es: Findlay compara las virtudes de Pablo con las cuatro virtudes ____ de la filosofía clásica.

questions.source_quote: It is interesting to compare the Apostle's definitions with Plato's celebrated scheme of the four cardinal virtues.

prompt.en: Findlay contrasts Pauline ethics with ____ ethics to explain their different priorities.
prompt.es: Findlay contrasta la ética paulina con la ética ____ para explicar sus diferentes prioridades.

questions.source_quote: The difference between the cast of the Platonic and Pauline ethics is most instructive.

prompt.en: Findlay names love and ____ as two distinguishing emphases of Christian moral character.
prompt.es: Findlay menciona el amor y la ____ como dos rasgos distintivos del carácter moral cristiano.

questions.source_quote: Love and humility are the two features whose predominance distinguishes the Christian from the purest classical conceptions of moral worth.

prompt.en: Findlay says some classical philosophers regarded a distinctive Christian virtue as a ____ rather than a virtue.
prompt.es: Findlay dice que algunos filósofos clásicos consideraban un rasgo distintivo del cristianismo un ____ y no una virtud.

questions.source_quote: The pride of philosophy regarded it as a vice rather than a virtue.

prompt.en: Findlay says the suddenness of a lapse should encourage a more ____ judgment that allows restoration.
prompt.es: Findlay dice que el carácter repentino de una caída debe fomentar un juicio más ____ que permita restaurar al hermano.

questions.source_quote: The suddenness, the surprise of his temptation is both a reason for more lenient judgment, and a ground for hope of his restoration.

prompt.en: Findlay warns against visiting a momentary offense with ____ severity.
prompt.es: Findlay advierte contra castigar una falta momentánea con severidad ____.

questions.source_quote: An offence committed in a rash moment, under provocation, must not be visited with implacable severity, nor magnified until it become a fatal barrier between the evil-doer and society.

prompt.en: Findlay says that restoring a wrongdoer demands self-restraint and ____.
prompt.es: Findlay dice que restaurar al que yerra requiere autodominio y ____.

questions.source_quote: The work of restoration needs a knowledge of the human heart, a self-restraint and patient skill, quite beyond their capability.

prompt.en: Findlay says restoration includes the offender's ____ into the Church, not only inner renewal.
prompt.es: Findlay dice que la restauración incluye la ____ del ofensor para la Iglesia, no solo su renovación interior.

questions.source_quote: The restoration here signified, denotes not only, or not so much, the man's inward, spiritual renewal, as his recovery for the Church, the mending of the rent caused by his removal.

prompt.en: Findlay moves from personal obligations to the ____ obligations of the Christian community.
prompt.es: Findlay pasa de los deberes personales a los deberes ____ de la comunidad cristiana.

questions.source_quote: Personal responsibility is the last word of the former paragraph; social responsibility is the first word of this.

prompt.en: Findlay says Paul chiefly wants spiritual ____ between teacher and hearers.
prompt.es: Findlay dice que Pablo desea sobre todo la ____ espiritual entre el maestro y quienes escuchan.

questions.source_quote: But it is spiritual fellowship that the Apostle chiefly desiderates.

prompt.en: Findlay warns that a merely ____ contribution may be the easiest part of the hearer's obligation.
prompt.es: Findlay advierte que la contribución meramente ____ puede ser la parte más fácil de la obligación del oyente.

questions.source_quote: Of that return the pecuniary contribution, the meed of "carnal things" with which so many seem to think their debt discharged, is often the least and easiest part.

prompt.en: Findlay explains the moral logic of sowing and reaping by appealing to the ____ of personal existence.
prompt.es: Findlay explica la lógica moral de sembrar y cosechar apelando a la ____ de la existencia personal.

questions.source_quote: It asserts the continuity of personal existence, the connection of cause and effect in human character.
